links.reason: The Tamil gives the women a vow to reach his feet 'அவ் உலகினில் நின் அடி அடைதும்' and the poem has no pyre argument; Vijayai and her unborn son appear in neither text, so teaches and gains lean on the epic's plot.
1663 bids the god 'வேழ மாகெனப் பணித்து விட்டான்' and 1664 shows the elephant; that is order and execution in sequence. The intent to frighten is the marker's inference, not a word of the verse.

The Kural woman says none names the leaver; the Ainkurunuru line ends 'அன்னாய்', so the speaker addresses the mother, not the girl, and the 'friend as the one voice' reading is unproved. 'பிரிந்தென' does name the cause, a real but thin contrast.

2927 'துறக்கத்திற் கேணி' makes giving a well in heaven, and Kural 222 says giving is good 'மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும்'; the contrast is real. But 222 does not deny a reward, so the epic's heaven is not shown to be 'an extra', and the Kural gains no school account from this verse.

'விதி வென்ற பரமன்' sets the lord over fate, against 'ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள'. The tension holds only if ஊழ் is read as karma, which the note never says, and the Kural question is rhetorical about worldly remedies.

2831 'அளவிற் புண்ணியம்' puts merit in measure of the gift, and Purananuru 134 refuses 'இம்மைச் செய்தது மறுமைக்கு ஆம்' as a trader's motive. The poem rejects a motive, not a doctrine of merit, so the two are not incompatible claims.

1987 ends 'மற்றோர் கதியே' and Naladiyar 11 has renunciation from foresight of grey hair 'நரைவரும் என்று'. Saying the other birth shows the renunciation is not fear of aging is the note's inference, and the epic adds no 'answer' to the wilderness.
Both are taunts about a bride or wives, but 1286 is about a maiden won by another and 769 about wives' sulks 'புலவி'; the shared theme is thin and both verses are flagged uncertain.

24 is a summary of the whole poem and 1951 shows the street scene. That she is 'paying no attention' is not in 1951, which only says she plays ball; the link is a fulfilment of the patikam, but the claimed reversal goes beyond the Tamil.

187 'கலத்தல் பான்மையில்' may mean only 'in the fitting way', and the note itself says 'if read as destiny'. 215 'முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை முளைத்து' is clearly destiny, so the shared cause rests on a doubtful reading.

1706 gives the norm 'அணிசுமந்து இருப்பது' in Nandattan's mouth, and Thirikadugam 66 'கொழுநனை இல்லாள் கறையும்' states unfit adornment. But கறை is itself uncertain (adornment or stain), and the epic only illustrates the rule.

129 'விரகினாற் பிரித்திடின்' has Yugi plan a stratagem because the king is 'போகத் தழுந்தலும்'; Kural 901 'மனைவிழைவார் மாண்பயன் எய்தார்' states the cost. They connect on theme, but the couplet offers no cure, so 'the couplet never considers' it adds nothing.

2555 asks 'என்னை தவஞ் செய்யா திகழ்ந்திருப்பது' on seeing his rise, and Naladiyar 53 argues from impermanence 'நிலையாமை'. The verse shows a rise, not failing goods, so the quatrain's list is not what the epic states.
Both are astrologer's findings (1451 'நாணப் பட்டான்' sign, 539 'இராசமா புரத்த'). The contrast of 'contest' for Gandharvadattai is not in 539, so teaches rests on facts outside the verse.
1010 has her credit the queen's 'அருளினன்றே துணிந்து எழுதிற்று'; there is no pride in 1001 or 1010 to turn into modesty. The pair is a painting begun and then presented.
Both parrots serve lovers, but in 1000 the parrot only answers 'சமழாது உரை'; the 'carries a plea across a distance' belongs to later verses. A repeated device with a thin shared use.
Both verses use eyes in city description (40 'மையரி மழைக்கண்ணார்', 44 bees mistaking eyes for flowers). The wishing tree in 40 belongs to the mansions, not the eyes, and 'ruling lords' is not in 40.

580 shows the sunk ship with the companions pointed out 'தோழர்ச் சுட்டிக் காட்டினான்'; 513 says the sea 'விழுங்க' the wealth and loved ones. A later verse that overturns the earlier is real, but Sitattan's grief is not in 513, so 'grief was real' is unsupported.

1614 has the queen smile and order Madhavan bound with garlands 'கோதைகளில் யாத்து'; her anger and the king's bow are not in the verse. Naladiyar 384 'உட்கி இடனறிந்து ஊடி' gives a standard, but the pair is an illustration.

1066 says begging, even for a cow's water, is the worst degrade, and 780 'இரந்துகோள் தக்கது' says such a death is worth begging for. The shared root is real, but 780 is hyperbole for how precious the death is, so it is a contrast of idiom, not clearly incompatible.

393 asks 'யாண்டு நேர் எல்லை... அழற்சி இன்மை' and Kural 303 says 'மறத்தல் வெகுளியை'. The contrast of a fixed term against forgetting is real, but nothing in the verse makes the teacher an ascetic, so the 'ascetic does not ask for it' clause is unsupported.
228 introduces Mananigai and 230 has her act; this is story order, which the graph records. The note says nothing the plot does not.
1068 sends the sun to see the rites and 1070 says they were done 'நிறைந்தார்'; this is sequence. The 'unseen wedding told through daybreak' reading is the marker's.

links.reason: Thirikadugam 1 names 'சொல்லின் அரில் அகற்றும் கேள்வியார்' and Kural 417 says the learned do not speak folly. The verse can mean the learned clear their own speech, so 'the virtue passes to the friend' is the note's reading.

1550 'ஆற்றுணாக் கொள்ளீர்' against Naladiyar 20 'தோட்கோப்புக் காலத்தால் கொண்டுய்ம்மின்' is a true shared image of provisions for the road of death, with the epic's kin-visit comparison. It is an echo of image, not a development.

170 names Urumannuvan telling the kings; neither a spy nor a second confirmation appears in it, and the marker says the teller may be the spies or the minister. The note depends on verse 169, which the Tamil here does not state.
Both use 'நோற்ற' language in love (1005 'மேகலை நோற்ற', 997 'செய்த வம்புரியாச் சிறியார்போல்'). It is a fair shared fancy that fortune is earned by penance, but the pairing teaches little beyond it.

1432 mocks leaf-hut ascetics who still embrace women 'முலைவள ராகந் தோய', and 1437 has them 'குடும்ப நீக்கி' and say their eyes are opened 'கண் விடுக்கப் பட்டேம்'; the later verse accepts the charge. That is a jibe and its answer, and teaches follows.

1453 feeds 'ஆயிரத் தெட்டு' guests daily for the bride's sake, and Kural 86 'வருவிருந்து பார்த்திருப்பான்' praises watching for guests. The epic's use is an instrument, a fair qualification, but the couplet is not 'shown to admit' hidden aims.

395 'என்போல் போற்று' has the chief hand the guest to his wife, and Kural 81 makes the household exist for guests. The poem enacts the rule; it adds the wife's place, but the pair is mostly illustration.

26 promises the uncle's daughter 'மாமன் மகள்' and 2460 names Govindan and the sacrificial hall 'வேள்விச் சாலை'. The king's gift-water in teaches is not in the verse, so the pairing is a plain fulfilment.
1577 'ஊன்பயில் குரம்பை' and 1584 'புழுப்பயில் குரம்பை' are one image by one speaker; the second is to the woman. That the rebuff was prepared in silent thought is read from order, not stated.

44 'வீடுநன் கடையு மென்றார்' promises the son's release and 157 has the father crown him and renounce. The marker's idea that the father takes the way promised for the son is wrong; only the first half is partly shown, so teaches adds only plot.
286 'நஞ்சின் துஞ்சும் வகை சூழ்ந்து' puts her fall to the poisoning plot and her deeds; 122 shows her love for the low man. The note calls hell the fruit of passion, which 286 does not say.
1948 asks 'ஐங்கணை வார்சிலை மைந்தனோ' and 1961 says he is 'மலரைங்கணை மைந்தன்'. Both are guesses at his likeness to Kama; 1961 does not answer the crowd, so 'answered' overstates it.
211 is the king's letter asking pardon 'பிழையது பொறுக்க', not an envoy's speech, and nothing in the verse shows brevity or smiling words 'நகச் சொல்லி'. The pairing stretches the couplet.
179 sends Varudakaran 'திறத்தினா லகற்று' and 180 has him drive the kings off. This is an errand and its result, and 179 itself says war began, so 'plan did not remove war' reads 180 into 179.
1112 'உருவத்தா லிருவ ராகி உள்ளத்தா லொருவ ரானார்' says two bodies one heart, and Kural 1122 'உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை'. Agreement with a slow-ripening image added; a modest, true pairing without a conflict.

Yasodhara 4 'மருவு வெவ்வினை வாயின் மறுத்து' and Kural 5 'இருவினையும் சேரா' both speak of deeds' clinging; the preface does not speak of devotion, so the epic does not 'limit' the couplet. The qualification is the note's.

19 praises the lord who ended 'செனித் திறக்கு மூப்பிறப்பு', which is his state; Kural 10 speaks of followers who cross 'பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல்'. The verse does not say what crossing consists of for others.

11 says women's perfumes weaken even ascetics 'நற்றவம் மேவி நின்றவரையும்', and Thiruppugazh 201 confesses craving for women. A shared theme, not a development; the Thiruppugazh text is hard to divide.

825 has the king revive at his son's words 'தானுயிர் தளிர்ப்பது', Kural 65 'சொற்கேட்டல் இன்பம் செவிக்கு'. The king's joy is relief at the news, not the pleasure of a child's speech as such.
